object_description: flat horizontal block-edge volume enclosing a central schoolyard
design_condition: The perimeter-enclosing volume is fitted to surrounding height differences and creates four use-specific outdoor spaces, including an introverted central schoolyard that is weakly connected to the neighborhood.

positive.statement: The flat, horizontally structured block-edge building is precisely fitted into the existing context by incorporating the surrounding height differences.

position.rationale: Continuous shallow perimeter mass is clearly visible in plan and all elevations.

positive.statement: The central schoolyard is the identity-creating center of the school complex and is accessed from various sides via spacious staircases.

position.rationale: The large central void is distinctly enclosed by the perimeter ring in the top view.

positive.statement: The internal organization is coherent and credibly implements the school's ‘under one roof’ principle.

position.rationale: Interior organization is not exposed, so the anchor uses the visible enclosing building surface.

positive.statement: The basic level is generously designed as an autonomous unit with flexible spaces, clear storage and short routes to the outdoor area.

position.rationale: Ground-level judgment is anchored to the southwest perimeter and lowest elevation band.

positive.statement: The ring-shaped primary-level access provides visual contact and great flexibility of use.

position.rationale: The inner perimeter indicates a ring circulation zone around the courtyard.

positive.statement: The shallow building depth allows good daylight quality in all rooms.

position.rationale: Very thin depth is consistently visible between the perimeter edges and elevation lines.

positive.statement: The hybrid construction has a positive effect on primary energy and greenhouse-gas emissions.

position.rationale: Construction and energy performance have no useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: It is questionable whether the courtyard can withstand the pressure of actual use and installations.

position.rationale: The central courtyard is clearly identifiable as the enclosed open void.

negative.statement: The introverted schoolyard is isolated from the neighborhood, barely visible and not very connected.

position.rationale: The enclosed central yard is visible, while neighborhood connection is not represented geometrically.

negative.statement: The urban integration of the existing gymnasium is also called into question.

position.rationale: The gymnasium is unnamed in the sample; an exterior perimeter anchor approximates the associated building area.

negative.statement: The desired elegance is not achieved equally on all facades, where vertical openings compete with the pronounced horizontality.

position.rationale: Elevation views show the horizontal facade bands and vertical interruptions.

negative.statement: The day-school access corridors appear too narrow, and the two music rooms have unfavorable proportions.

position.rationale: Corridors are interior and indistinguishable; placement is constrained to the southwest building edge.

negative.statement: The large surface area of the building shell and extensive terrain movements have a negative impact on operational and gray energy.

position.rationale: The broad shell is visible; terrain movement is approximated near the low perimeter edge.

negative.statement: The project has increased construction costs, particularly because of comparatively high land consumption.

position.rationale: Cost and land-consumption judgment has no useful single spatial marker.
